- **self**: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines (14/7)

## Structure and components

- [statement] High ANN recall establishes fidelity to exact vector neighbors, not semantic relevance or end-to-end output quality. Qdrant separates these evaluation layers, and Elastic distinguishes mathematical recall from relevance. (high confidence) — https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/ · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines · also: https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/recall-vector-search-quantization, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04522

## How it works

- [statement] The June 3, 2026 preprint ANN Search: Recall What Matters argues that strict neighbor-set overlap can impose unnecessary computation when alternative neighbors have nearly identical distances. Its abstract reports downstream quality remaining stable despite falling Recall@k and proposes inverse approximation ratio as an additional utility proxy; this is a research finding, not a universal replacement rule. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04522 · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines · also: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.04522

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Use exhaustive exact search as the reference and run ANN with the same query criteria. MongoDB's worked comparison preserves the query vector, vector field, filter and result limit; Elastic's demonstration compares optimized search with a full-Float32 flat-search reference. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines · also: https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/recall-vector-search-quantization

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Increasing ANN search effort can improve overlap with ENN while increasing query latency and compute consumption. Compare resource use and cost at a common recall target rather than comparing default settings alone; the cost comparison is an evaluation recommendation, not measured savings. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines · also: https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/, https://engineering.fb.com/2017/03/29/data-infrastructure/faiss-a-library-for-efficient-similarity-search/
- [statement] Use representative workload queries rather than a single example. MongoDB recommends a set of 100 example queries; Qdrant describes a typically 20–50 query sample. These are tutorial sample sizes, not statistical guarantees that production tails are covered. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines · also: https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/
- [statement] The inspected ANN-Benchmarks implementation counts returned distances within the exact kth-neighbor distance plus a default epsilon of 0.001, then averages the count divided by k. This distance-tolerant measure can differ from strict ID overlap; declare the evaluator and tolerance when comparing benchmark results. (low confidence) — https://github.com/erikbern/ann-benchmarks/blob/main/ann_benchmarks/plotting/metrics.py · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines
- [statement] Evaluate a representative set of queries rather than treating one successful query as evidence of overall recall. Both MongoDB and Qdrant describe multi-query comparisons and aggregated overlap evaluation. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines · also: https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/
- [statement] For a platform TCO comparison, an evidence-based methodology is to compare speed and memory at a shared accuracy target, rather than assuming the fastest configuration provides equivalent retrieval fidelity. This recommendation follows Faiss's speed-memory-accuracy framework and the documented search-effort trade-offs. (medium confidence) — https://engineering.fb.com/2017/03/29/data-infrastructure/faiss-a-library-for-efficient-similarity-search/ · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md, https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Construct ENN ground truth with exhaustive similarity evaluation, then compare ANN results for the same query criteria. In cross-platform evaluation, keeping vectors, similarity function, query set and eligible corpus equivalent is a methodological prerequisite for attributing differences to approximation. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines · also: https://engineering.fb.com/2017/03/29/data-infrastructure/faiss-a-library-for-efficient-similarity-search/, https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/recall-vector-search-quantization
- [statement] For two full top-k result sets, ID-overlap recall@k is |ANN_k intersect ENN_k| / k. Average it across test queries; nine shared IDs out of ten means recall@10 = 0.9. This set metric does not evaluate ranking within those shared IDs. (high confidence) — https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/ · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines · also: https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/recall-vector-search-quantization, https://engineering.fb.com/2017/03/29/data-infrastructure/faiss-a-library-for-efficient-similarity-search/
- [statement] Jaccard similarity is intersection divided by union, whereas top-k overlap recall divides by k. For equal-sized top-k sets with overlap m, Jaccard = m/(2k-m), so recall = 2J/(1+J). Nine shared results at k=10 yield recall 0.9 but Jaccard about 0.818; this conversion follows algebraically from the cited definitions. (high confidence) — https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.spatial.distance.jaccard.html · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines · also: https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/, https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/recall-vector-search-quantization
- [statement] Elastic explicitly scopes its recall example as a very small-scale demonstration and advises testing on the user’s own data. Its example is not evidence that Atlas and separate infrastructure meet identical recall, latency or cost requirements at production scale. (low confidence) — https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/recall-vector-search-quantization · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines
- [statement] Increasing search effort trades resources and latency for closer agreement with exact results: MongoDB discusses increasing numCandidates, and Qdrant discusses increasing hnsw_ef. Measure the resulting recall and latency together. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/vector-search/query/improve-accuracy.md · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines · also: https://qdrant.tech/documentation/tutorials-search-engineering/ann-recall/
- [statement] The June 3, 2026 preprint ANN Search: Recall What Matters reports that downstream classification and RAG quality can remain stable while Recall@k falls, and proposes inverse approximation ratio as an alternative utility proxy. This is a research finding, not a universal replacement rule; only its abstract was inspected. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04522 · keywords: Measuring ANN recall against ENN baselines
